Saved raw/law/ch322.html, raw/law/gl21-43A.html.
cadence: Approved January 12, 2021; s.1 effective 540 days after passage; regulations due within 1 year.
history: No amendment to s.43A found: the May 2025 snapshot of the codified section matches the 2020 Act text (2-hour, 8-hour, 24-hour, May 15 provisions all present).
status_reason: Primary legal basis for every MA discharge notice; deadlines quoted in report.
notes: Key text: 'A permittee shall issue an updated public advisory every 8 hours for an ongoing discharge and within 2 hours when a discharge ceases or is projected to cease'; (c) 'As soon as possible, but no later than 2 hours after the discovery of a discharge'; (i) DEP website to display current discharges 'posted within 24 hours of the department receiving such data'; (j) annual report 'Not later than May 15 of each year'.

name: MassDEP CSO API behind the portal (eeaonline.eea.state.ma.us/dep/CSOAPI/api/)
access_detail: Unauthenticated JSON. Endpoints read from the app bundle and called 2026-11-01: GET Incident/GetIncidentsBySearchFields/?[ReporterClass=&EventType=&Municipality=&OutfallId=&WaterBody=&PermiteeClass=&PermiteeName=&VolumeOfDischargeFrom/To=&RainfallDataFrom/To=]&pageNumber=1&pageSize=N&&orderBy=incidentDate%20desc (pageSize 1000 accepted; orderBy submittedDate also works; IncidentFromDate/IncidentToDate returned HTTP 500 in every format tried). GET Incident/GetIncidentById?id={incidentId} (adds compliance self-check answers, parentIncidentId, attachment list, and personal fields reporterName/createdBy/modifiedBy which must be dropped). GET Incident/GetChildIncidentsByParent?id=...&pageNumber=1&pageSize=10& (updates such as 'Ceased'). GET Metadata/GetMetadataForIncident (enumerations: reporterClass, eventType, permiteeClass, municipality list). GET Incident/GetIncidentsForExcel/?{same filters} returns xlsx (26 columns). GET Attachment/GetActiveAttachments?id=... lists the attached advisory (.eml or .pdf); Attachment/Download/{incidentId}/{fileExternalId} returned HTTP 500. GET Permitee/GetPermiteeDetails?permiteeName=... returns the permittee's WWTP outfall with lat/lon only. Requests without Origin/Referer headers returned HTTP 500; with Origin https://eeaonline.eea.state.ma.us and the portal Referer they returned 200.

name: Connecticut River Conservancy 'Is It Clean?' (isitclean.us, formerly connecticutriver.us)
waters_covered: Connecticut River watershed sites in MA and VT (CRC lab: 'over 80 locations'); MA sites incl. Chicopee River and tributaries in Chicopee/Springfield, mainstem sites
access_detail: Webflow site; site records are embedded in the map page HTML as data attributes (data-slug, data-waterbody, data-watershed, data-town, data-state, data-latitude, data-longtitude, data-date, data-quality, data-clean-dry/-wet, data-boat-dry/-wet, data-not-clean-dry/-wet). First page holds 100 sites (pagination ?663469da_page=2). Scripts on cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ryan-ctriver/iic-prod@1.6.4; a Heroku endpoint is-it-clean-089e6447542b.herokuapp.com/api/v1/weathers supplies weather only. Saved raw/watershed/iic-map.html, iic-sample-sites.json.
fills_event_fields: monitoring: waterbody, coordinates, sample date, E. coli value (quality)
cadence: 'Monitoring typically occurs from late May to October'; 'Results are posted to this site's map within 24 hours after the sample was taken' (how-it-works page). Search results: weekly sampling at 13 MA and 8 CT locations.
history: Multi-year; the first page's Chicopee sites show 2021 dates (stale sites retained).
status_reason: The only public bacteria results for the Springfield-Holyoke-Chicopee reach; categories 'Clean for swimming' / 'Clean for boating only' / 'Not clean for either'. Numeric cut-offs are drawn as images, not text; ask CRC for a data export or API.
notes: CRC's own analysis (search result) says the Holyoke-Chicopee-Springfield stretch tends to have the highest E. coli levels and names CSOs as the main suspected cause.

name: Charles River Watershed Association Flagging Program and Public Flagging API
operator: Charles River Watershed Association (site built by Code for Boston)
waters_covered: Lower Charles River Basin, model reaches 2-5, boathouses
access_detail: Open JSON, no key: /api/v1/model (hourly E. coli predictions per reach with 'safe' boolean, model_version, time_returned) and /api/v1/boathouses (boathouse, latitude, longitude, reach, safe, overridden, reason). Swagger docs linked from /api. Email alerts (crwa.org) and Twitter @crwaflagging. Saved raw/watershed/crwa-model.json (trimmed), crwa-boathouses.json.
fills_event_fields: advisories: authority, coordinates (boathouse), started_at/valid time (UTC), advice (safe flag), reason (override text, e.g. CSO or cyanobacteria)
cadence: Hourly model; flags shown in boating season only. On 2026-11-01 the site said the database had not updated in at least 24 hours and it was not boating season.
history: API returns the latest 24 hours; history via model inputs endpoints (not read).
license: 'the CRWA allows open access to its Public Flagging API' (API page).
status_reason: Best ready-made advisory feed in MA: red flags downstream of any Lower Basin CSO in the past 48 hours, during cyanobacteria blooms, or when modelled E. coli exceeds the standard.
notes: Quote: 'If any Combined Sewer Overflow (CSO) discharges took place in the past 48 hours in the Lower Basin, red flags will be flown downstream of the CSO discharge point.'
